result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

arguments.reason: The simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test (SYN-AQP-UPDATE) does not address consumer perceptions of tap water safety or willingness to pay for a branded purifier. It tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under a conditional supply assumption, which does not provide evidence for or against T1.

arguments.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes water safety and purity, particularly in markets where tap water is perceived as unsafe or unhealthy. Begin with a targeted pilot to test purchase intent and willingness to pay before scaling.
arguments.target_customer: Consumers in regions where tap water quality is uncertain or perceived as unsafe, such as areas with high bottled-water consumption or where water safety concerns are prominent.
arguments.value_proposition: A branded home water purifier that promises purity and safety, leveraging Aquaporin's membrane technology to address consumer concerns about water quality.
arguments.next_action: Run the proposed Consumer Messaging Test (online survey with safety-focused vs. safety-reliability messaging) to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay before committing to a full-scale launch.
arguments.uncertainty: The extent to which consumers will actually purchase a branded purifier based on safety perceptions remains uncertain; the test will provide critical data to resolve this.
would_change_if: If the pilot shows purchase intent below a threshold (e.g., <10%) or willingness to pay significantly below the price of a generic membrane unit, the investment would be reconsidered in favor of a different strategy.

tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.
tool_result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

result.title: Simulated home-barista learning proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 32 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 72 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.

In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 32 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 72 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.

tool_result.title: Simulated home-barista learning proposition test
tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 32 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 72 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.
tool_result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 32 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 72 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.

X1.sample: 300 U.S. adults who have expressed interest in home coffee equipment (recruited via panels), balanced for age, gender, and self-reported coffee consumption frequency.

arguments.name: Differentiated vs. Convenience Messaging Test
arguments.method: Online survey with simulated purchase offers for two Simonelli machine concepts: (1) a differentiated home barista model emphasizing social ritual and identity (e.g., "Create your own third place coffee experience"), and (2) a convenience-focused model emphasizing quick, easy prep for busy lifestyles (e.g., "Espresso in 30 seconds, no expertise needed"). Participants view each concept and indicate willingness to pay.
arguments.sample: 300 U.S. adults who have expressed interest in home coffee equipment (recruited via panels), balanced for age, gender, and self-reported coffee consumption frequency.
arguments.measure: Willingness-to-pay (WTP) on a 1‑10 scale for each concept, and self-reported importance of social ritual vs. convenience as a purchase criterion.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Higher average WTP for the differentiated concept (social ritual) and higher proportion of participants citing social ritual as the primary purchase reason.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Higher average WTP for the convenience concept (quick prep) and higher proportion of participants citing convenience as the primary purchase reason.

result.title: Simulated home-barista learning proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 72 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 32 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

arguments.reason: The simulated result (SYN-SIMO-UPDATE) tests the incremental effect of a learning offer among home espresso enthusiasts, not the demand for a differentiated Simonelli proposition. It does not address the social ritual mechanism of T1, so the theory remains unchanged.
arguments.new_claim: Home barista consumers will adopt a differentiated Simonelli consumer proposition because they value the social experience of coffee preparation and the ability to create a personal ritual, leading them to purchase premium equipment that signals status and community belonging.

arguments.recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. The evidence shows a broader consumer market decline (Simonelli's own financial data) and no specific demand for a differentiated Simonelli proposition. Continue monitoring market trends and conduct a small-scale test before committing resources.

arguments.next_action: Run the proposed differentiated vs. convenience messaging test (300 U.S. adults, €18,000, 8 weeks) to measure willingness-to-pay and purchase intent differences before any new investment.
arguments.uncertainty: The overall consumer market is declining, and there is no direct evidence of demand for a differentiated Simonelli proposition. The test will resolve whether the social ritual mechanism (T1) or convenience mechanism (T2) drives purchase.
would_change_if: If the test shows a willingness-to-pay difference of at least €15 between the differentiated and convenience concepts, indicating strong social ritual demand, we would proceed to develop a differentiated proposition targeting home barista.

tool_result.title: Simulated home-barista learning proposition test
tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 72 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 32 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.
tool_result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

X1.name: Consumer Preference Test: Home Barista vs. Home Coffee Machine
X1.method: Online survey with a choice-based conjoint test. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. Group A sees a home barista machine (professional-grade espresso machine) and is asked to indicate willingness to pay a premium price. Group B sees a home coffee machine (simplified, easy-to-use machine) and is asked to indicate willingness to pay a premium price. Both groups are asked the same price point and a
X1.sample: 300 adult consumers aged 25-55 who have purchased coffee equipment in the past 12 months, recruited via an online panel. Stratified by region to ensure geographic diversity.
X1.measure: Willingness to pay (WTP) for each product, measured as the maximum price participants would pay. Secondary measure: stated intent to purchase on a 7-point scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show a significantly higher average WTP and purchase intent than Group B, indicating demand for a home barista machine.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show a significantly higher average WTP and purchase intent than Group A, indicating demand for a home coffee machine.

X1.decision_rule: If the difference in average WTP between the two groups is at least €20 (a threshold derived from a pilot test showing a €15 difference is a meaningful purchase decision), we conclude that the product aligned with the theory (T1 or T2) is

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home barista culture, but first validate demand through a low-cost test. If the test shows a meaningful willingness-to-pay premium for a home barista machine, proceed to develop and launch a consumer product; otherwise, maintain the current professional portfolio.
final.target_customer: Home baristas and coffee enthusiasts who enjoy the ritual and quality of espresso at home.
final.value_proposition: A home barista machine that offers professional-grade espresso making with ease of use, design, and a structured learning experience, positioned as the ultimate home coffee ritual.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Consumer Preference Test (choice-based conjoint survey) to measure willingness to pay and purchase intent for a home barista machine versus a home coffee machine.
final.uncertainty: The actual willingness to pay for a home barista machine and Simonelli's ability to capture value from such a product are uncertain. The test will resolve this uncertainty.
would_change_if: If the test shows no meaningful willingness-to-pay premium for a home barista machine, the recommendation would shift to maintain the current professional portfolio.
If additional evidence shows a sustained decline in consumer demand for coffee equipment, the recommendation would also shift to maintain the current portfolio.

result.title: Simulated installation-coordination offer test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 72 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 32 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 72 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 32 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

result.title: Simulated installation-coordination offer test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 72 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 32 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

tool_result.title: Simulated installation-coordination offer test
tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 72 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 32 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

result.title: Simulated installation-coordination offer test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 32 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 72 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.
